claims.claim_text: The indexed Major Henry A. Murray is the Harvard psychologist who led the first OSS Station S assessment program.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, indexed major rank, Harvard intelligence-service chronology, and NPS Station S identification align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Harvard dates a temporary wartime departure for Army intelligence work; NPS identifies Murray at OSS Station S.
claims.match_notes: The combination of name, rank, profession, institution, and specific OSS assignment is highly discriminating.

claims.claim_text: Murray's immediate wartime affiliation before or concurrent with his OSS assignment was the U.S. Army.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard states that he left temporarily for Army service and worked with American intelligence agencies; NARA indexes him as a major.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Henry A. Murray.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded wartime pathway; the exact Army-to-OSS administrative transition is not stated.
claims.match_notes: The Army relationship is not labeled a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The Harvard Psychological Clinic was Murray's last documented civilian institutional affiliation before wartime Army and OSS work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard documents his clinic career and temporary wartime departure; NPS identifies him in OSS as being of the Harvard Psychological Clinic.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Henry A. Murray.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded immediately before wartime service, though exact payroll and leave dates require archival confirmation.
claims.match_notes: The clinic is treated as employment and research affiliation, not merely education.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Conyers Read is the University of Pennsylvania historian who led the OSS Research and Analysis British Empire unit.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, civilian P-8 index grade, Penn chronology, and CIA description of his OSS leadership align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Penn documents COI leave in 1941-1942 and subsequent OSS leadership.
claims.match_notes: The rare name and exact institutional and OSS role evidence make a namesake collision unlikely.

claims.claim_text: Read's immediate pre-OSS government affiliation was the Coordinator of Information.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Penn finding aid places him on COI staff during academic year 1941-1942 before identifying his OSS section leadership.
claims.match_notes: COI is modeled as a government assignment and kept distinct from OSS.

claims.claim_text: The University of Pennsylvania was Read's last civilian employer before wartime federal intelligence service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Penn dates his professorship from 1934 and identifies a leave for COI work in academic year 1941-1942.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded by faculty appointment and wartime leave.
claims.match_notes: The professor role is employment; it is not inferred merely from education.

claims.claim_text: Read held senior management posts at William F. Read and Sons Company from 1920 through 1933.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Penn finding aid documents his progression from treasurer to vice-president and general manager and then president.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment ending before his 1934 Penn appointment.
claims.match_notes: This earlier business career is not presented as the immediate predecessor to OSS.

claims.claim_text: The indexed CAF-14 employee Donal McLaughlin is the architect and graphic designer who served in the OSS Presentation Branch.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name, high civilian grade, CIA design role, and scholarly OSS career chronology align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The scholarly source explicitly dates his move from Loewy's office to OSS in 1942.
claims.match_notes: The rare name and exact design role provide strong identity resolution.

claims.claim_text: McLaughlin left Raymond Loewy's industrial design office to join OSS in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The University of Minnesota Press study states the employer-to-OSS transition directly.
claims.match_notes: The historical office wording is preserved rather than replaced with a later firm name.

claims.claim_text: Raymond Loewy's industrial design office was McLaughlin's last civilian employer before OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly chronology identifies Loewy's office as the position McLaughlin left for OSS in 1942.
claims.match_notes: The same evidence answers both immediate affiliation and last civilian employer because no intervening assignment is documented.

claims.claim_text: McLaughlin worked in Walter Dorwin Teague's design office before joining Raymond Loewy's office.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly source places Teague's office immediately before Loewy's in McLaughlin's prewar design career.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; exact dates are not stated.
claims.match_notes: This earlier employer is not mislabeled as immediate.

claims.claim_text: McLaughlin undertook prewar design work for the National Park Service before later federal and private design posts.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly career chronology describes a short stint drawing maps and park structures for the National Park Service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar government assignment; exact dates are not stated.
claims.match_notes: Separate Treasury and Resettlement Administration affiliations are retained in the structured timeline.

claims.claim_text: McLaughlin designed post offices for the Treasury Department before his private design-firm work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly chronology names the Treasury Department and the post-office design assignment.
claims.match_notes: This is not presented as a civilian employer or immediate predecessor.

claims.claim_text: McLaughlin prepared plans for greenbelt towns for the Resettlement Administration.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly chronology directly identifies the agency and planning work.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar government assignment bounded by the agency's 1935-1937 existence.
claims.match_notes: The historical New Deal agency is retained under its own name.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lincoln Lundquist is architect and industrial designer Oliver Lincoln Lundquist.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The unusual surname and indexed given name match Lundquist's middle name; CIA, UN, and scholarly sources identify the full name and exact OSS design role.
claims.temporal_assessment: The scholarly chronology places his War Department and OSS work from 1941 onward.
claims.match_notes: The index omits Oliver, but the exact Lincoln Lundquist name components and distinctive OSS design role are corroborated independently.

claims.claim_text: Lundquist's probable immediate pre-OSS affiliation was presentation work for the War Department beginning in early 1941.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly source places him at the War Department early in 1941 and later in the OSS Presentation Branch.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Oliver Lincoln Lundquist.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate sequence; exact OSS transfer or enlistment date is not supplied.
claims.match_notes: Published with visible qualification and excluded from default high-confidence immediate-affiliation analytics.

claims.claim_text: Raymond Loewy's industrial design office was Lundquist's last documented civilian employer before War Department and OSS work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The scholarly chronology dates his Loewy-office work from 1937 and his War Department arrival to early 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Oliver Lincoln Lundquist.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before the intervening government assignment.
claims.match_notes: The Loewy office is identified as the last civilian employer, not the immediate OSS predecessor.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain William J. Morgan is psychologist William James Morgan, formerly Anthony J. Mitrano.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NARA's name and captain rank, NPS's full name and OSS psychologist role, the official Senate alias note, and Yale's 1937 Mitrano listing align.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS dates his OSS work to 1943-1944; the Senate record confirms the same wartime identity.
claims.match_notes: The alias resolution is supported by an official Senate record and an institutional Yale graduate list, not genealogy or model memory.

claims.claim_text: Before World War II, Morgan worked as a school psychologist in Rochester and the Bronx.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Washington Post obituary documents the occupation and locations but does not identify the employing school systems or establish which was last.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for William James Morgan based on education, occupation, Army, OSS, and alias evidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar occupation; employer identity and final sequence remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: No employer is inferred from the locations. No reliable named pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.
